scenes.title: The 1848 Cavendish Railroad Rock-Cut Blast
scenes.era: September 13, 1848, 4:30 p.m., Rutland and Burlington Railroad rock cut near Cavendish, Vermont

layout.description: An open-air New England granite railroad cut carved into a wooded hillside. Pale blasted granite ledges rise on both sides of a raw dirt and rubble railbed, with a timber derrick and wooden platform car in the pit a few feet behind the rock shelf.

positions.where: Centre foreground on a flat granite shelf directly above a vertical drilled blasting hole
positions.facing: Body angled toward the drilled hole, head turning sharply over his right shoulder toward his crew in the pit behind him

positions.where: Left foreground beside a wooden black-powder keg and clay-sand pail
positions.facing: Facing Gage, reaching for the sand scoop

positions.where: Background pit near the timber derrick and wooden platform car
positions.facing: Facing Gage, calling out and lifting granite blocks

props.name: Tamping iron
props.period_detail: Hand-forged cylindrical iron bar, 3 feet 7 inches (110 cm) long, 1.25 inches (3.2 cm) thick, tapering over 12 inches to a 0.25-inch point, weighing 13.25 pounds, worn smooth from use
props.physical_behavior: Drops pointed-end first into the un-sanded granite hole, strikes a bright orange spark against the rock wall, and shoots vertically upward like a rocket through Gage's left cheek and out the top of his skull, arcing high into the air and thudding onto the granite rubble 20 to 25 yards behind him

props.name: Drilled granite blasting hole and black powder charge
props.period_detail: Deep narrow cylindrical bore drilled vertically into the grey granite ledge, filled with coarse black blasting powder and a braided hemp fuse, missing its protective sand plug
props.physical_behavior: Flashes bright orange-white and erupts in a dense plume of white black-powder smoke and flying granite dust

props.name: Wooden black-powder keg and sand bucket
props.period_detail: Coopered oak powder keg with iron hoops resting beside a wooden bucket of pale tamping sand
props.physical_behavior: Rattles and tips on the rock ledge as shockwave dust scatters across the stone

actions.verb_sequence: Grips the 3-foot-7-inch iron tamping bar vertically over the drilled granite hole, twists his head over his right shoulder toward his men, and drives the pointed iron bar down into the un-sanded hole
Flinch and duck behind the platform car as the charge explodes, then sprint forward across the rubble toward Gage

reactions.reaction: Jolts backward from the upward blast and collapses onto his back across the granite ledge, his hands clutching toward his left cheek as white smoke billows around his shoulders
Drop their iron pry bars, recoil with raised hands shielding their faces, and drop to their knees beside the fallen foreman

scenes.wardrobe: 1840s New England railroad work clothes: Gage in rolled-up white linen shirtsleeves, dark buttoned waistcoat, heavy canvas trousers with leather braces, and a broad-brimmed felt work hat knocked off by the blast; workmen in dust-stained cotton shirts, vests, and leather boots
scenes.lighting: Crisp late-afternoon New England sunlight raking across pale granite walls, punctuated by the sharp orange-white flash and sunlit white black-powder smoke plume
scenes.recognition_hook: A 1840s railroad foreman tamping black powder into a granite hole with a 3-foot-7-inch iron rod turns his head, sparks the rock, and the rod blasts straight up through his left cheek and skull.

key_visual.description: the tamping iron shoots straight up through the porcelain foreman's left cheek below the eye and out the top of his frosted-glass cranium, clean white porcelain chips scattering

scenes.title: Sitting Upright in the Ox Cart and Greeting Dr. Harlow
scenes.era: September 13, 1848, 5:00-6:00 p.m., dirt road and Joseph Adams's hotel porch in Cavendish, Vermont

layout.description: A rutted New England dirt road leading up to the wooden veranda and long front staircase of Joseph Adams's tavern-hotel in Cavendish.

positions.where: Sitting upright on the wooden bench of a two-wheeled ox cart halted beside the hotel steps
positions.facing: Facing Dr. John Harlow and Dr. Edward Williams at the foot of the veranda stairs

positions.where: Standing beside the ox cart wheel holding his leather medical bag
positions.facing: Facing Gage, leaning in to inspect the wound

positions.where: Standing by the wooden yoke of the oxen and at the rear tailboard of the cart

props.name: Two-wheeled wooden ox cart and hotel ledger
props.period_detail: Rough-plank 1840s New England ox cart with tall spoked wooden wheels and iron rims
props.physical_behavior: Creaks and settles as Gage swings his boots over the tailboard and steps down onto the gravel road

props.name: Linen head bandage and doctor's leather bag
props.period_detail: White linen cloth wrapped around the top of Gage's head and Dr. Harlow's brass-clasped black leather medical satchel
props.physical_behavior: Harlow snaps open the brass clasp of his medical bag on the porch steps while Gage lifts his hand to touch his left cheek

actions.verb_sequence: Rides sitting upright in the wooden ox cart, grips the wooden side rail, steps down onto the road, and walks steadily up the wooden hotel stairs while touching his left cheekbone
Sets his leather medical bag onto the porch rail, snaps open the brass clasp, and steps beside Gage to support his elbow

reactions.who: Dr. John Martyn Harlow and bystanders
reactions.reaction: Freeze in disbelief with shoulders stiffened and hands raised half-open as the injured foreman walks upright up the stairs and speaks coherently

scenes.wardrobe: Gage in his singed white linen shirt and dark waistcoat with a white linen bandage wrapped around his crown; Dr. Harlow in a dark 1840s wool frock coat, high collar, and cravat
scenes.lighting: Clear golden-hour daylight across the clapboard hotel porch and dirt road
scenes.recognition_hook: Minutes after the iron bar pierced his skull, Phineas Gage sits upright in an ox cart, climbs the hotel stairs, and calmly tells Dr. Harlow how the iron passed through his head.

scenes.title: Impulsive Outburst in a Cavendish Tavern and Refusal of the Foreman Job
scenes.era: Spring 1849, Cavendish, Vermont tavern and railroad contractor office

layout.description: A timber-beamed 1849 Vermont tavern and contractor pay room with heavy oak tables, pewter tankards, and a railroad work-schedule ledger spread open near sunlit multipane windows.

positions.where: Standing at the centre oak table, leaning forward on both fists
positions.facing: Facing the railroad contractor and former crewmen across the table

positions.where: Behind the oak table beside the open work ledger and inkstand
positions.facing: Facing Gage, pulling the ledger back

positions.where: Beside the tavern bench to the right

props.name: Pewter tavern mug and oak table
props.period_detail: Heavy 1840s pewter tankard and thick plank oak tavern table
props.physical_behavior: Topples over and clatters across the oak tabletop, spilling amber ale across the wood when Gage slams his fist down

props.name: Railroad contractor ledger and quill pen
props.period_detail: Leather-bound railroad crew roster and payroll ledger
props.physical_behavior: Slams shut as the contractor pulls it away from Gage's reach

actions.verb_sequence: Slams his fist onto the oak tavern table, knocks over a pewter mug, and shoves his wooden chair backward when refused his foreman post
Slams the leather roster ledger shut and slides it back across the desk away from Gage

reactions.reaction: Recoil a step backward from the table, folding their arms and shaking their heads as Gage storms toward the door clutching his iron rod

scenes.wardrobe: 1849 New England civilian clothes: Gage in a wool waistcoat, white shirt, and dark trousers with his left eyelid drooped shut; contractor in a dark broadcloth coat
scenes.lighting: Bright daylight streaming through multipane tavern windows with floating dust motes
scenes.recognition_hook: Friends and bosses say he is 'no longer Gage' as the once-calm foreman slams a tavern table in a sudden burst of temper and loses his old job.

scenes.title: Driving a Six-Horse Stagecoach in Chile and the 1850 Daguerreotype Pose
scenes.era: 1850-1859, Boston daguerreotype studio and the Valparaiso-to-Santiago mountain road in Chile

layout.description: Sunlit mountain coach road between Valparaiso and Santiago, Chile (paired with the 1850 portrait studio composition): a wooden Concord-style stagecoach hitched to six horses on a dusty coastal mountain road.

positions.where: Perched high on the wooden driver's box of the stagecoach (and seated upright in the portrait frame)
positions.facing: Facing forward down the mountain road, holding the separated leather reins of six horses in his hands with his tamping iron secured beside the seat

positions.where: Stepping into the coach door below and loading leather trunks onto the roof rack
positions.facing: Looking up toward Gage on the driver's box

props.name: Six-horse leather reins and wooden Concord stagecoach
props.period_detail: Heavy leather multi-rein harness attached to six porcelain carriage horses pulling a painted wooden stagecoach with iron-rimmed wheels
props.physical_behavior: The leather reins snap taut in Gage's hands, the heavy wooden coach wheels roll forward kicking up golden dust, and the coach lanterns sway in rhythm

props.name: Inscribed iron tamping bar
props.period_detail: The smooth 3-foot-7-inch tapered iron rod held upright between Gage's knees as in his 1850 daguerreotype portrait
props.physical_behavior: Gleams in the bright sunlight as Gage grips the iron bar upright against his shoulder

actions.verb_sequence: Climbs onto the high wooden stagecoach box, gathers the six leather reins cleanly between his fingers, and flicks the reins to drive the six-horse team smoothly along the road

reactions.reaction: Gage sits tall with squared shoulders and steady hands while passengers nod and settle calmly into the rolling coach

scenes.wardrobe: Well-kept 1850s attire matching the Wilgus daguerreotype: tailored dark vest, crisp collar and cravat, dark trousers, and wide-brimmed Chile driver's hat, with his left eyelid closed
scenes.lighting: Bright high-altitude Andean daylight with crisp shadows and golden road dust
scenes.recognition_hook: Far from the textbook myth of a ruined drifter, a well-dressed Phineas Gage drives a six-horse stagecoach in Chile and poses proudly with the iron bar that pierced his skull.

scenes.title: Harvard Warren Anatomical Museum Skull, Tamping Iron, and CT Connectome Mapping
scenes.era: 1868 to 2012, Warren Anatomical Museum at Harvard Medical School and modern neuroimaging lab

layout.description: Bright museum gallery at Harvard's Warren Anatomical Museum with a glass display case holding Gage's exhumed skull with its hinged forehead bone flap, the 1850 plaster life mask, and the 110-cm tapered iron rod on brass cradles.

positions.where: Standing beside the glass museum case and a sunlit examination table
positions.facing: Facing the mounted skull and tamping iron, aligning the rod along the left cheek-to-forehead trajectory

props.name: Exhumed Phineas Gage skull and 110-cm tamping iron on brass stand
props.period_detail: Real human skull specimen with entry defect beneath the left zygomatic arch and healed exit opening in the superior frontal bone, paired with the 3-foot-7-inch tapered iron bar
props.physical_behavior: The brass turntable rotates smoothly in the light as the scientist aligns the tapered rod beside the left cheekbone entry path

actions.verb_sequence: Lifts the tapered steel rod from its brass cradle, aligns it beside the left cheekbone of the mounted skull model, and rotates the brass stand

reactions.reaction: Lean forward over the glass display table, bracing their hands on the rim in quiet amazement as the left-sided trajectory lines up

scenes.wardrobe: Crisp museum curator / researcher attire: tailored blazer and white laboratory coat
scenes.lighting: High-key museum gallery daylight with clean specular highlights on the glass case and brass stand
scenes.recognition_hook: At Harvard's Warren Museum, Gage's actual skull and 3-foot-7-inch tamping iron sit side by side, allowing modern CT and connectome scans to map the exact left-frontal wiring the rod severed.
